decision.analysis: Round 3/3 (final). The prior results establish a clear hierarchy: resnet18 (0.9924) > residual_cnn (0.9770) > vision_transformer (0.9628) > compact_transformer (0.9521) > tiny_cnn (0.9304). The resnet18's second run peaked at epoch 6 (vs epoch 3 for others), indicating it was still improving and may benefit from more training headroom. Key observations: (1) standardize normalization is universal across all configs; (2) hflip is the common augmentation, with vflip appearing in the top-2 results; (3) all used adamw + cosine + batch 128 + wd 0.0001; (4) class_weighting was false everywhere despite 1.63x imbalance — this is an unexplored lever; (5) label_smoothing was 0.05 in most, 0.0 in tiny_cnn. For the final round, I will: (A) push resnet18 with modestly increased capacity (depth 4, hidden 48), lower LR for stability, class weighting to address imbalance, and extended patience to capture the late-training gains seen at epoch 6; (B) test a deeper residual_cnn (depth 5, hidden 48) with broader augmentation (hflip+vflip+brightness) and larger batch (256) to see if the residual architecture can close the gap to resnet18. Both avoid excessive weight decay (0.0001) and stay within the lightweight parameter budget appropriate for 28×28 pathology tiles.

candidates.rationale: Extends the best prior result (resnet18, 0.9924 at epoch 6) by: (1) increasing hidden 32→48 and depth 3→4 for ~30% more capacity to capture finer nuclear/glandular morphology; (2) lowering LR 5e-4→3e-4 for more stable convergence with the added parameters; (3) enabling class_weighting to directly address the 1.63x imbalance (classes range 7.9K–12.9K samples), which was untested in all prior runs; (4) raising label_smoothing 0.05→0.1 for better-calibrated probabilities on the 9-class problem; (5) increasing dropout 0.1→0.15 as a mild regularizer for the extra capacity; (6) extending early_stopping_patience to 8 epochs since the prior best peaked at epoch 6, giving the model room to continue improving. Augmentations (hflip+vflip) and standardize normalization are retained from the winning config. Weight decay stays at 1e-4 to avoid over-regularizing the already well-performing architecture.

Pushes the residual_cnn (prior best 0.9770) toward the resnet18 ceiling by: (1) increasing depth 3→5 for richer hierarchical feature extraction (nuclear texture → gland boundaries → tissue architecture) while skip connections maintain gradient flow; (2) widening hidden 32→48 for more channel diversity; (3) adding vflip and brightness augmentations (3 total) to increase effective training diversity — brightness is safe for pathology as it simulates staining variation; (4) enabling class_weighting to counter the 1.63x imbalance, particularly helping the minority classes (7.9K, 8.0K samples); (5) raising batch_size to 256 for lower gradient variance and more stable training of the deeper network; (6) increasing dropout to 0.2 to regularize the additional depth; (7) keeping LR at 5e-4 (between the 1e-3 that underperformed and the 3e-4 that is more conservative) with cosine decay. This tests whether a well-tuned residual CNN can approach resnet18 performance at lower parameter cost, providing a useful capacity-efficiency data point.
